title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff during regional failover
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: During the incident on 2026-02-16 we observed SLO enforcer thrashing when region-level capacity signals flapped. This PR stabilizes backoff ordering and makes the regional failover path idempotent so that overlap windows don't cause concurrent aggressive shedding. Changes: 1) Add a compare-and-swap guard to SLO enforcer backoff state transitions so a stale backoff delta cannot overwrite a more recent backoff (slo/enforcer/backoff_manager.go). 2) Smooth the backoff decay curve by limiting step-downs to one tier per evaluation window to avoid immediate re-acceptance of traffic after a short spike (slo/enforcer/policy.go). 3) Add regional-runlock around failover orchestration to ensure we don't run overlapping failover workflows for the same customer (slo/enforcer/failover_coordinator.go). 4) Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent backoff signals and an end-to-end canary test that runs against the perf-canary harness. Testing & verification: Local unit tests added, CI canary runs against a two-region emulation in perf-canary. Observability: Add diagnostic gauge 'slo_enforcer.backoff_version' and a trace span for 'failover.orchestrate' so we can correlate backoff changes with failover actions. Rollout plan: squash-merge to main, deploy to canary region for 1 hour, then gradual rollout to other regions with monitoring alerts enabled (ENG-3241). Backport: will open follow-up PR to release branch if canary is green. Related: references incident SUP-1124 and postmortem notes.
